read: full: pp.1-14 (abstract, introduction, related work, design requirements, architecture, held-out generator, task set, evaluators and metrics, reproducibility, experiments, limitations, conclusion) read in full; references and appendix catalogue pp.14-19 skimmed.
venue_now: arXiv 2606.20950v2 [cs.AI], 2 Jul 2026 (page 1 stamp); no venue; repository on GitHub and artifact archived on Zenodo (p.9)
what_it_is: An executable benchmark for AI agents in electric power engineering: 41 task families in eight areas (network analysis, short circuit and protection, stability and grid code, distributed resources, microgrids and dispatch, reliability and restoration, power quality and standards, forecasting), each grounded in a cited standard, textbook method or article (pp.1, 7-8). An agent reads a task file and writes a structured JSON solution; a deterministic evaluator recomputes the engineering quantities, checks hard constraints and returns a feasibility flag, a score relative to the reference optimum and a list of violations, while the agent's rationale is recorded but not scored (pp.2, 5, 8). Held-out cases are synthesized on demand by per-family perturbation generators under a private seed, so the construction is public but the instances are not (pp.6-7). A June 2026 reference round with three command-line agents gives near-ceiling scores (public means 0.951-0.973, held-out 0.973-1.000), and a grid of four further models under two harnesses spreads from 0.44 to 0.93 (pp.10, 12).
domain: engineering: electric power systems (one sub-discipline of electrical engineering, none of EngTrace's three electrical domains)
size: 41 task families with one public case each, in eight areas (pp.7, 12); one generated held-out case per family per round (p.10); 328 generator-validation variants (41 x 8, p.11); three reference agents plus four models under two harnesses (pp.9-12)
source_of_items: engineering literature (standards such as IEC 60909, textbook methods, articles), written as compact executable cases by the author; held-out cases generated by perturbing each public case under a private seed (pp.6-8)
instances: generated (the held-out split, per round from a private seed); the public split is a fixed set of 41 cases
has_gold_traces: no: reference solvers compute the reference answer or optimum; there are no reference intermediate steps, and the agent's rationale is excluded from scoring (pp.2, 8)
evaluation: deterministic evaluators of the structured final output, not of reasoning: feasibility against hard constraints, a score normalised to the reference optimum (exact quantities at 0.1% relative tolerance with a small absolute floor, optimisation tasks by objective gap, classification by exact sets, compliance pass/fail), and explicit violations; feasible rate, perfect rate and mean score per run (pp.8-9)
human_validation: No human study. Each task was checked for physical correctness against its cited source before inclusion (p.7); each family declares a provenance confidence (11 high, 28 medium, 2 low; p.8); three evaluators are cross-checked against hand-derived golden cases (p.9). Unanimous agent failures were used to find specification defects and an evaluator bug (pp.10-11).
contamination_measures: private-seed generators: held-out cases are never distributed, only aggregate run summaries are published, and a seed is spent once a round is disclosed (pp.6-7, 13); public and held-out scores are compared, and held-out scores are not lower (p.10)

engtrace_use.explanation: Not cited in the May paper. Paragraph: engineering, or the introduction's contamination sentence. It is the one engineering benchmark in this batch that already uses EngTrace's contamination design: per-family generators with a public mechanism and a private seed (pp.6-7), as EngTrace's revised pool does (private 128-bit seed, hashed manifest). The revision should present the private-seed pool as shared practice, citing this paper, not as a novelty. What EngTrace must say it adds: this benchmark scores the structured outcome and excludes the reasoning (p.2), has no gold traces, covers one sub-discipline with one public case per family (p.12), and validates its evaluators only against three hand-derived golden cases (p.9); EngTrace checks the intermediate steps of free-form traces against code-derived milestones across five branches, with a residual judge validated against experts.

suggested_wording: In power engineering, the Power Systems Agent Benchmark (Trashchenkov, 2026) recomputes the quantities in an agent's structured answer with deterministic evaluators and synthesizes held-out cases from a private seed, but it scores the answer, not the reasoning that produced it.
facts_to_cite: 41 task families in eight areas of power engineering, each grounded in a cited standard, textbook method or documented formulation (pp.1, 7).

Agents return structured solutions; deterministic evaluators recompute the engineering quantities, check hard constraints and return a feasibility flag, a score in [0,1] relative to the reference optimum and a list of violations; the agent's rationale is recorded but not scored (pp.2, 5, 8).

About half the evaluators compute a quantity in closed form from a standard or textbook method; the rest score decisions over simplified surrogate models; none yet uses a power-system simulator (p.6).

Held-out cases are produced on demand by per-family physics-aware perturbations of the public case under a private random seed, accepted only if the reference solver solves them and the solution is feasible and locally optimal; only aggregate summaries are published (pp.6-7).
Provenance confidence per family: 11 high, 28 medium, 2 low (p.8); three evaluators are cross-checked against golden cases derived by hand (p.9).
Exact quantities are scored with a 0.1% relative tolerance (pp.8-9).

Reference round (June 2026): Codex with gpt-5.5, Cursor with composer-2.5 and OpenCode with deepseek-v4-flash-free reach public mean scores of 0.951-0.973 and held-out means of 0.973-1.000; no agent scores lower on held-out cases (p.10).
Unanimous agent failures exposed specification defects and an off-by-one evaluator bug that self-consistency checks missed, because solver and evaluator share code (pp.10-11).
All 328 generated validation variants (41 x 8) were feasible, and 40 of 41 families gave eight distinct instances (p.11).
One case per family per split, and sampling variance is not estimated (pp.12-13).
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: engineering content with deterministic recomputation of engineering quantities (p.8); instances generated from a private seed for contamination resistance (pp.6-7); tolerance-based exact checks (0.1%, pp.8-9); an evaluator-defect quality-control step (pp.10-11) that parallels EngTrace's certification. Lacks: any process or step evaluation (rationale unscored, p.2); gold traces; expert validation of the evaluators (three hand-derived golden cases only, p.9); multi-branch scope (power systems only); statistical depth (one case per family per split, no sampling variance; pp.12-13). Its subjects are tool-using agents with structured outputs, not reasoning traces.
notes: Paragraph: engineering (or the introduction's contamination sentence). Priority: should, not must; it is outcome-level, single-author and confined to one sub-discipline, so a reviewer is unlikely to require it; but it is the precedent to cite wherever the revision presents the private-seed pool, and the consolidator may raise it to must on that ground. The paper itself places private-seed generation in the family of dynamic benchmarks (p.4), so the idea is not its invention either. Naming: search_engineering_web.md describes the same paper (arXiv 2606.20950) under the key trashchenkov2026powersystemsagent, but candidates/engineering_web.json has no entry for it; the batch key trashchenkov2026psab comes from engineering_arxiv.json. Its caution that 'a reference answer derived from an evaluator cannot certify it' (pp.11, 13) applies to any benchmark whose gold answers come from the code that checks them, EngTrace's templates included; EngTrace's answer to it is the experts' hand-solving in certification.
